hurdle_name: Outlier units that could not be clustered by HDBSCAN.
Mandatory consignment-wise inspection schemes and heightened EU border controls impose strict health certification requirements on spice and marine exports.
Indian authorities mandated laboratory testing on imported Nepali tea which led buyers to suspend purchases and disrupted cross-border trade.
Pack-house and cold-chain infrastructure is concentrated in a few districts, leaving exporters outside those clusters without EU-compliant post-harvest facilities.
EUDR compliance mandates extensive collection and assessment of geolocation and traceability data which imposes heavy processing burdens on exporters.
Ministerial discourse and press coverage encouraging the fisheries sector to develop internal production quality and value-added export capabilities rather than raw commodities.
Rice exporters suffer from inadequate post-harvest infrastructure including scientific storage and modern transport logistics which degrades grain quality and disrupts exports.
Macro-level trade discourse highlighting government initiatives and free trade agreements without detailing operational firm-level compliance friction.
European corporate sustainability directives mandate statutory reporting disclosures and complex environmental assurance procedures across supply chains.
Aggregate national export volume and value reporting that functions as a press-release cluster rather than identifying specific MSME supply chain barriers.
Statutory hygiene and sanitary regulations mandate specific facility standards and waste disposal practices that challenge the infrastructure capability of petty operators.
Academic literature and frameworks exploring the use of monitoring technologies and multi-actor collaboration to identify modern slavery in supply chains.
